rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿadhāb names pain whose suffering persists; the verse uses it for punishment threatened against deniers who turn away.
rows.anchor: العذاب : اسم لما استمر ألمه

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Fāris says the word’s original sense in Arabic is striking or beating.
rows.anchor: قال ابن فارس : وأصل العذاب في كلام العرب : الضرب

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Exegetes use al-ʿadhāb for the prescribed penalty for adultery; examples include the half penalty and the liʿān passage.
rows.anchor: فعليهن نصف ما على المحصنات من العذاب

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Here al-ʿadhāb refers to transformation of the wrongdoers into apes and swine.
rows.anchor: والثاني : المسخ . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: In the pen sūra, al-ʿadhāb refers to the destruction of wealth.
rows.anchor: والثالث : هلاك المال . ومنه قوله تعالى في نون والقلم

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The warning to Noah’s people uses al-ʿadhāb for drowning.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الغرق . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The punishment from above or beneath is glossed as stoning and the earth swallowing people.
rows.anchor: والخامس : القذف والخسف

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: In these passages al-ʿadhāb means hunger, including the distress that prompts the people to cry out.
rows.anchor: والسادس : الجوع . ومنه قوله تعالى في المؤمنين

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Al-ʿadhāb can mean killing; some identify the lower punishment in 32:21 with the killing at Badr.
rows.anchor: والسابع : القتل . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحشر

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: In the messengers’ threat, al-ʿadhāb means painful beating or assault.
rows.anchor: والثامن : الضرب المؤلم . ومنه قوله تعالى في يس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waqaʿa is a past-tense verb; its basic image is falling from a higher place to a lower one.
rows.anchor: وقع : فعل ماض ، والأصل فيه : السقوط من العلو إلى السفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase waqaʿa kadhā can also mean that something happened; mawāqiʿ al-ghayth are places where rain falls.
rows.anchor: ويقال : وقع كذا ، بمعنى : كان . ومواقع الغيث : مساقطة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: In the verse about the sky, waqaʿa means to fall down.
rows.anchor: أحدها : بمعنى سقط . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحج

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: In the Hour’s name and the other cited warnings, waqaʿa means occurred or came to pass.
rows.anchor: والثاني : بمعنى كان . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: At the contest with Moses, waqaʿa means became manifest: truth prevailed and their work failed.
rows.anchor: والثالث : بمعنى بان . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: When the word comes upon them, waqaʿa means became due or inevitable.
rows.anchor: والرابع : بمعنى وجب . ومنه قوله تعالى في النمل

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: In the mountain passage, waqaʿa means descended upon them, referring to punishment.
rows.anchor: والخامس : بمعنى نزل . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hawā means to fall; Ibn Fāris cites the verb hawā yahwī and related nouns for a pit or sequential falling.
rows.anchor: هوى : بمعنى سقط . قال ابن فارس : يقال : هوى الشيء يهوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-hāwiya is both a name for Hell and a general term for a deep pit; hawwā means descending, while hawat ummuhu is an insult.
rows.anchor: والهاوية : اسم من أسماء جهنم . والهاوية أيضا : كل مهواة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: In the oath by the star and in the overturned town passage, hawā means descended.
rows.anchor: أحدها : بمعنى نزل . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: In the warning about God’s anger, hawā means perished.
rows.anchor: والثاني : بمعنى هلك . ومنه قوله تعالى في طه

words: تهوي به الريح في مكان سحيق
rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: In the image of the wind carrying someone away, tahwī means goes or is borne away.
rows.anchor: والثالث : بمعنى الذهاب . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ordinary usage, ahl means relatives by blood who are bound by kinship and mutual support; by contextual indication it can be used figuratively.
rows.anchor: الأهل في عموم التعارف : الأقارب من العصبة وذوي الأرحام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man’s ahl are his household; manzil āhil describes a home with its people, and the verb can mean to marry.
rows.anchor: ويقال : منزل آهل إذا كان به أهله . وأهل فلان ، يأهل ويأهل أهولا : إذا تزوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexical note also gives ihāla as melted fat and says istaʾhala al-rajul means he ate it.
rows.anchor: والإهالة : للودك المذاب . وأستأهل الرجل : أكلها

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Ahl can mean the inhabitants of towns; the cited example also includes hypocrites of Medina.
rows.anchor: أحدها : ساكنو القرى . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Ahl al-kitāb means the people who follow the scriptures.
rows.anchor: والثاني : قراء الكتب . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Ahl can mean a woman’s guardians or masters; the same sense appears in the command to return trusts to their people.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الأرباب . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Ahl can refer to a wife, as in Moses travelling with his family.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الزوجة . ومنه قوله تعالى في القصص

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Ahl can mean children or immediate family carried aboard the ark.
rows.anchor: والخامس : الأولاد . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Ahl can mean one’s religion or religious community, as Noah’s son was excluded from his ahl.
rows.anchor: والسادس : الدين . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: In the command to establish prayer at home, ahl means the community or household under one’s care.
rows.anchor: والسابع : الأمة . ومنه قوله تعالى في طه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Ahl can mean a person’s people and clan, as in appointing arbiters from both spouses’ families.
rows.anchor: والثامن : القوم والعشيرة . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Ahl can describe those qualified for or entitled to something.
rows.anchor: والتاسع : المستعدون للشيء . ومنه قوله تعالى في الفتح

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Ahl can mean the one deserving something; the Prophet explains God as deserving worship without a partner and forgiveness for those who avoid association.
rows.anchor: والعاشر : المستحق . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥaqq means what is sound and correct, opposite falsehood; ḥaqīqa is the true outcome of a matter, and ḥaqqa means became due.
rows.anchor: الحق : الصواب والصحيح ، وضده : الباطل . والحقيقة : ما يصير إليه حق الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ḥāqqa describes disputants each claiming truth; when one prevails, ḥaqqahu or aḥaqqahu is used, as is iḥtaqqū for mutual claims.
rows.anchor: وحاق فلان فلانا : إذا خاصمه وادعى كل واحد منهما الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥāqqa names the Resurrection because it befalls all; ḥiqqa names a camel old enough to be ridden, and ḥuqāq is its plural.
rows.anchor: والحاقة : القيامة ، لأنها تحق بكل . والحقة : من أولاد الإبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The familiar box is called ḥuqqa, plural ḥuqaq; ḥaqḥaqa is the hardest, most exhausting pace for a rider’s back.
rows.anchor: والحقة : معروفة ، والجمع : حقق . والحقحقة : أرفع السير وأتعبه للظهر

rows.speaker: مطرف بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Muṭarrif’s verse witnesses ḥaqḥaqa as exhausting travel, contrasting it with moderation as the best course.
rows.anchor: قال مطرف بن عبد الله : إن خير الأمور أوساطها ، وإن شر السير الحقحقة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: One Qur’anic sense of al-ḥaqq is God Himself.
rows.anchor: أحدها : الله تعالى ، ومنه قوله تعالى في المؤمنين

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Al-ḥaqq can mean the Qur’an, as in passages describing the truth coming to the rejecters.
rows.anchor: والثاني : القرآن ، ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنعام

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Al-ḥaqq can refer to Islam, including the command to establish it and the statement that the Prophet stands upon clear truth.
rows.anchor: وفي النمل : ﴿ إنك على الحق المبين

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Al-ḥaqq can mean justice or a just judgment.
rows.anchor: الرابع : العدل . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Al-ḥaqq can mean monotheism, as in passages affirming that truth belongs to God and rejecting those who deny it.
rows.anchor: الخامس : التوحيد . ومنه قوله تعالى في المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zawj is one of two matched things of the same kind and can name either member; a man or woman may each be called zawj.
rows.anchor: الزوج : ما ( كان ) له قرين من جنسه

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Fāris says zawj can mean a kind or variety of plant.
rows.anchor: قال ابن فارس : والزوج [ من ] النبات اللون

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Zawj can mean a companion or counterpart; the cited judgment scene gathers wrongdoers with their satanic associates.
rows.anchor: أحدها : القرين . ومنه قوله تعالى في الصافات

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains the pairing of souls as each being joined with its counterpart in Paradise or Hell.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : قرنت بأشكالها في الجنة والنار

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Zawj can mean a species or category, including livestock, plants, and other created kinds.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الصنف . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنعام

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Zawj can mean wives or spouses.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الزوجات . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root’s basic sense is humiliation and diminished worth; hawn, with fatḥa on hāʾ, instead means calmness and dignity.
rows.anchor: فأما الهون . بفتح الهاء - فهو السكينة والوقار

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Hawn can mean something small or insignificant.
rows.anchor: أحدها : الصغر . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النور

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Hawn can mean easy or effortless.
rows.anchor: والثاني : السهل . ومنه قوله تعالى في مريم

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: In the warning that God may abase someone, the root means humiliation.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الذل . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحج

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Mahīn can mean weak or lowly, describing the fluid from which humans are created.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الضعف . ومنه قوله تعالى في المرسلات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naṣr means help; intişār means taking revenge. Naṣr can also mean rain or coming to a place, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: النصر : العون وانتصر فلان : انتقم . والنصر : المطر . والنصر : الإتيان

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited poem uses unṣurī to mean come to or visit a land.
rows.anchor: إذا ودع الشهر الحرام فودعي … بلاد تميم وانصري أرض عامر

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Naṣr can mean protection or prevention from punishment; the cited passages ask who can shield people from God’s torment.
rows.anchor: أحدها : المنع . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Naṣr can mean aid, including God’s support for those who support His cause.
rows.anchor: والثاني : العون . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحج

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Naṣr can mean victory over an enemy.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الظفر . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Naṣr can mean retaliating or taking vengeance after suffering wrong.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الانتقام . ومنه قوله تعالى في عسق

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses hudā as guidance and guidance as clarification.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة الهدى : الإرشاد ، والإرشاد : البيان

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says the root sense of hudā in Arabic is divine enabling or success.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن الأنباري : أصل الهدى في كلام العرب : التوفيق

rows.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
rows.claim: Some scholars connect hadiyya, a gift, with guiding or correcting affection; hawādī are the foremost visible necks of a troop of horses.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض أهل العلم : أن الهدية سميت هدية لأنها تدل على تقويم الوداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexical entry also uses hudā for leading the bridal procession, sacrificial livestock sent to the sanctuary, and walking between two people for support.
rows.anchor: وتقول : أقبلت هوادي الخيل ، إذا بدت أعناقها

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Hudā can mean clear explanation or guidance made manifest.
rows.anchor: أحدها : البيان . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Hudā can mean the religion of Islam; the target verse’s straight guidance is included in this grouping.
rows.anchor: والثاني : دين الإسلام . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Hudā can mean faith, which God increases in the guided and which opponents may reject.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الإيمان . ومنه قوله تعالى في الكهف

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Hudā can mean calling or directing people toward the right way; the cited examples include Quranic guidance to the straight path and right judgment.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الدعاء . ومنه قوله تعالى في الرعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawt is an event that ends life; mawta is one death, and mawāt or mawātān can describe death among livestock or uncultivated land.
rows.anchor: الموت : حادث تزول معه الحياة . والموتة : الواحدة من الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry also uses mawta for a madness-like fit and names Muʾta as the place where Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib was killed.
rows.anchor: ومؤته - بالهمز . أرض بها قتل جعفر

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Mawt can mean ordinary death, as experienced by every soul.
rows.anchor: أحدها : الموت نفسه . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Mawt can mean the semen stage; the first of two deaths is being a drop before life.
rows.anchor: والثاني : النطفة . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Mawt can mean misguidance, from which God brings a person into life and guidance.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الضلال . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنعام

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Mawt can describe drought or barren land; every dead land in the Qur’an means uncultivated earth.
rows.anchor: الرابع : الجدب . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Mawt can mean war, as in the challenge to those who had wished to face it.
rows.anchor: والخامسة : الحرب . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Mawt can refer to inanimate idols, which are not alive.
rows.anchor: والسادس : الجماد - ومنه قوله تعالى في النحل

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Mawt can mean disbelief, with the dead person understood as a disbeliever; some fold this into the semen sense.
rows.anchor: والسابع : الكفر . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some add plague as an eighth sense of death; Ibn al-Jawzī rejects treating the noun itself as a synonym for plague.
rows.anchor: وقد ألحق بعضهم وجها ثامنا فقالوا : والموت : الطاعون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās’s explanation is that they feared death by plague, which had already come upon them.
rows.anchor: وإنما معناه حذر الموت بالطاعون ، لأنه كان قد نزل بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yamīn can mean either an oath or the familiar bodily member opposite the left hand.
rows.anchor: اليمين : تقال ويراد به الحلف . وتقال ويراد بها العضو المعروف

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Yamīn can mean the right hand itself, as in Moses’s question.
rows.anchor: أحدها : العضو المعروف الذي تماثله الشمال . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة طه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Yamīn can mean the direction on the right side.
rows.anchor: والثاني : جهة اليمين التي هي هذا العضو المعروف

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Yamīn can mean strength or power.
rows.anchor: والثالث : القوة . ومنه قوله تعالى في الصافات

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Yamīn can mean an oath, including vows people swear by God.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الحلف . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة والمائدة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Yamīn can mean a covenant or pledged undertaking.
rows.anchor: والخامس : العهد . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة براءة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Yamīn can mean the religion’s direction or approach; the devils approach people from the side of religion to cause doubt.
rows.anchor: والسادس : الدين . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: In mā malakat aymānukum, yamīn is treated as an extra connective expression: the phrase means those whom your right hands possess.
rows.anchor: والسابع : أن يكون صلة ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jawzī selected material from earlier wujūh works, excluded unsuitable items, and added acceptable transmitted exegetical material.
rows.anchor: فهذا آخر ما انتخبت من كتب الوجوه والنظائر التي رتبها المتقدمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He deliberately retained some distinctions that a rigorous critic might combine, reasoning that merging them would erase most of the traditional categories.
rows.anchor: وقد تساهلت في ذكر كلمات نقلتها عن المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says comparison between chapters reveals the book’s value; its linguistic derivations are meant to sharpen understanding, and he asks God for benefit and sincere reward.
rows.anchor: وما ذكرت في كتابي هذا من الكلمات اللغوية في اشتقاق الكلمة وما يتفرع منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A bayt is a shelter from heat and cold; in settled construction it is a walled plot with a roof, while nomads use a circular wool structure with a matching roof.
rows.anchor: البيت : ما يأوي إليه الإنسان ليقيه الحر والبرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say bayt is named for being suitable for spending the night; bayāt and tabyīt refer to a night attack, and bāta means doing something at night.
rows.anchor: وقيل : سمي بيتا لأنه يصلح للبيتوتة فيه . والبيات والتبييت أن يأتي العدو ليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayyata al-amr means planning a matter at night; buyūt can mean a troubling concern occupying its owner.
rows.anchor: والبيوت : الأمر يبيت عليه صاحبه ، مهتما به

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The unnamed poet’s line uses bayyatū for a plan made at night.
rows.anchor: أتوني فلم أرض ما بيتوا … وكانوا أتوني بشيء نكر

rows.speaker: الهذلي
rows.claim: The Hudhalī poet uses buyūt for a distressing matter one fears.
rows.anchor: إذا خفت بيوت أمر عضال

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Bayt can mean an ordinary built house or dwelling.
rows.anchor: منه قوله تعالى في النور : ﴿ لا تدخلوا بيوتا

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Bayt can mean a mosque or place of worship.
rows.anchor: والثاني : المسجد ، ومنه قوله تعالى في يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Noah’s prayer, bayt means his ship.
rows.anchor: والثالث : السفينة ، ومنه قوله تعالى [ في نوح ]

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative gloss takes Noah’s bayt as his religion.
rows.anchor: أي : سفينتي ، وقيل ديني

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Bayt can refer to the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الكعبة ، ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Bayt can mean a tent or portable shelter.
rows.anchor: والخامس : الخيمة ، ومنه قوله تعالى في النحل

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Bayt can mean a prison or confinement.
rows.anchor: والسادس : السجن ، ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Bayt can mean a nest or hive, as in the bee and spider passages.
rows.anchor: والسابع : العش ، ومنه قوله تعالى في النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwā is relying on what creates a barrier between oneself and what one fears; the muttaqī guards against the thing feared.
rows.anchor: التقوى : اعتماد المتقي ما يحصل به الحيلولة بينه وبين ما يكرهه

rows.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
rows.claim: The author’s teacher says taqwā is more commendable than faith because faith may be mixed with other things, whereas taqwā is not.
rows.anchor: وقال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwā is taking precautions; waraʿ is avoiding a doubtful matter, whose cause is conjectural, and restraining oneself from uncertain consequences.
rows.anchor: ويقارب التقوى الورع إلا أن الفرق بينهما أن التقوى أخذ عدة والورع دفع شبهة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Taqwā can mean affirming God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: أحدها : التوحيد ، ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Taqwā can mean sincerity of heart.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الإخلاص ، ومنه قوله تعالى في الحج

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Taqwā can mean worship and obedience; the Pharaoh passage asks why they do not worship God.
rows.anchor: والثالث : العبادة ، ومنه قوله تعالى في النحل

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Taqwā can mean refraining from sin.
rows.anchor: والرابع : ترك المعصية ، ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Taqwā can mean fear or reverence; Noah, Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, and Shuʿayb use it in exhortations to their people.
rows.anchor: والخامس : الخشية ، ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufr means covering or concealing; Ibn Fāris also calls remote, rarely visited land kufr, with its inhabitants ahl al-kufūr and villages al-kufūr.
rows.anchor: قال ابن فارس : والكفر - بفتح الكاف ما بعد من الأرض عن الناس

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited poetic line uses kafara for clouds covering the stars.
rows.anchor: في ليلة كفر النجوم غمامها

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Kufr can mean disbelief in God’s oneness, the most common Qur’anic sense.
rows.anchor: أحدها : الكفر بالتوحيد . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Kufr can mean ingratitude for a blessing; Moses’s rebuke is read in this sense.
rows.anchor: والثاني : كفران النعمة . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Kufr can mean disavowing or disowning one another on the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: والثالث : التبري . ومنه قوله تعالى في العنكبوت

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Kufr can mean denial or rejection of something recognized.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الجحود . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Kuffār can mean farmers, because they cover seed with earth.
rows.anchor: والخامس : التغطية . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Firār fundamentally means flight; mafar is the place a fugitive reaches, al-farr are the fleeing people, and farartu ʿan al-amr means I avoided it.
rows.anchor: الأصل في الفرار : أنه الهرب . والمفر : المكان الذي ينتهي إليه الفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The related verb iftarr can describe a man showing his teeth while laughing; a horse’s farāra eye is striking enough to reveal its quality.
rows.anchor: وافتر الرجل ضاحكا ، إذا أبدى أسنانه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Firār can mean fleeing, including escape from death or killing.
rows.anchor: أحدها : الهرب . ومنه قوله تعالى في الشعراء

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Firār can mean aversion from something one dislikes, such as death.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الكراهة . ومنه قوله تعالى في الجمعة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Firār can mean turning away and not attending to someone.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الالتفات . ومنه قوله تعالى في عبس

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Firār can mean keeping away or increasing one’s distance.
rows.anchor: والرابع : ( 96 / ب ) التباعد

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil adds a fifth sense: flight to God means repentance.
rows.anchor: وألحق مقاتل وجها خامسا ، فقال : الفرار : التوبة
